title: Kalaignar Karunanidhi and Poet Kannadasan: Poetic Wit, Political Rivalry, and Mutual Adoration
summary: Though frequently clashing in electoral politics, Chief Minister M. Karunanidhi and Poet Laureate Kannadasan exchanged peerless poetic repartees rooted in mutual literary genius.
keywords: Historical Dialogue 163: நேரு: “முதல் முறை என்பது முறை அல்ல; பார்த்துக்கொண்டிருப்பது”
full_text:
In the 1960s and 70s, the Tamil literary and political landscape was electrified by the dazzling interplay between DMK stalwart M. Karunanidhi and the legendary lyricist-poet Kaviarasu Kannadasan.

Having begun as comrades in the Dravidian movement, political cross-currents later placed them on opposing sides. Kannadasan frequently published biting poetic barbs in newspapers, and Karunanidhi countered in his daily 'Murasoli' epistles with equal literary flair.

At a grand literary symposium in Chennai, both giants shared the stage before thousands of eager connoisseurs.

Taking the podium first, Kannadasan looked at Karunanidhi with a mischievous glint and remarked in verse:
"Karunanidhi is my cherished friend, yet in statecraft he possesses the cunning of a fox!"

When Karunanidhi rose to respond, the audience held its breath. Grasping the microphone, Karunanidhi smiled broadly:
"Our revered Kaviarasu has compared me to a fox. I take no offense, for folklore recognizes the fox as an animal of sharp intellect! But what shall I compare our dear poet to? He is undoubtedly like a majestic lion! Yet there is one curious difference: while the king of the jungle roars through strength, our poetic lion roars through enchanting verses—only to drift gently wherever the political winds happen to blow during election season!"

The audience erupted in delight. Kannadasan was so thoroughly amused by Karunanidhi's brilliant literary retort that he rose from his seat, walked over, and embraced Karunanidhi with roaring laughter.

Their rivalry was conducted not in bitterness, but in the soaring stratosphere of classical Tamil wit and mutual affection.
